prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Summary of Reform UK’s 2024 “Contract”

Core aims
- Freeze most immigration; end small-boat crossings via detention, offshore processing and returns; tighten asylum and criminal deportations.
- Eliminate NHS waiting lists via workforce incentives, use of independent capacity and patient vouchers.
- Cut personal taxes (raise income tax threshold to £20,000; higher rate from £70,000), reduce energy taxes and levies, and expand domestic oil and gas.
- Reduce government waste and regulation; support SMEs and self-employed; simplify tax.
- Strengthen policing, justice, defence and critical infrastructure.

Key policies by area

Immigration
- Freeze non-essential migration; bar student dependants; five-year residency/employment before benefits.
- Detain and deport illegal entrants; exit ECHR; create a Department of Immigration; deny legal aid to non-citizens.
- Employer immigration tax: raise NI to 20% for foreign workers (small firms and essential health/care exempt).
- Estimated savings: £5–10bn pa; employer tax revenue £4bn pa.

Government spending and waste
- Stop paying interest on QE reserves to banks (£35bn pa saving).
- 5% efficiency/waste cut across departments (£50bn pa).
- Halve foreign aid (£6bn pa); improve HMRC collection; deregulate retained EU laws.
- Potential savings: £91bn pa.

Economy – personal
- Lift income tax threshold to £20,000; cut energy taxes (fuel duty -20p/litre; scrap VAT and green levies on energy).
- Cut stamp duty (0% to £750k; 2% to £1.5m; 4% above).
- Restore VAT-free tourist shopping.
- IHT: no tax below £2m; 20% above (charity alternative).
- Cost: £70bn pa.

Economy – business
- No corporation tax on profits up to £100k; main rate 25%→20% (then 15% in year 3).
- Abolish IR35; raise VAT threshold to £150k.
- Abolish business rates for high-street SMEs, offset by a 4% online delivery tax; entrepreneurs’ tax to 5%.
- Planning reform; large-scale deregulation and tax simplification.
- Cost: £18bn pa.

NHS
- Zero basic-rate tax for frontline NHS/social care staff for 3 years; expand training; write off student fees via service.
- Use independent/overseas capacity; 20% tax relief on private healthcare/insurance.
- Patient vouchers if GP/consultant/operation waits exceed 3/3/9 weeks; efficiency measures; “Pharmacy First” drive; charge for missed appointments.
- Cost: £17bn pa.

Energy/Net Zero
- Scrap Net Zero targets and related subsidies; fast-track North Sea and shale pilots; expand SMRs and other tech.
- Claimed savings: £30bn pa.

Policing and justice
- +40,000 officers over five years; zero-tolerance approach; more stop and search; tougher drug and knife penalties.
- Justice budget £10bn→£12bn; redefine hate crime; build 10,000 prison places; reforms on grooming gangs, youth training camps.
- Costs: Policing £3bn pa; Justice £2bn pa.

Education
- Curriculum revisions; restrict gender identity measures in schools; single-sex facilities.
- 20% tax relief on independent school fees; scrap interest on student loans; raise entry standards; expand PRUs; optional 2-year degrees.
- Cost: £5bn pa.

Benefits and work
- Tighten assessments (face-to-face); “two-strike” rule for job offers; incentives and apprenticeships to move up to 1m+ into work.
- Savings: £15bn pa.

Brexit and constitutional changes
- Scrap retained EU law; abandon Windsor Framework; prepare to renegotiate TCA.
- Leave ECHR; reform Human Rights Act; reform House of Lords and civil service leadership; tighten postal voting; PR referendum; British Bill of Rights.
- Cost: neutral.

Defence
- Spend 2.5% of GDP by year 3 and 3% by year 6; pay review; legal protections; dedicated veterans department; procurement reform.
- Cost: £14bn pa.

Housing
- Fast-track brownfield; prioritise locals for social housing; restore buy-to-let mortgage interest relief; leaseholder protections.
- Cost: neutral.

Children/families
- Larger transferable marriage allowance (when affordable); front-load child benefit ages 1–4; regulate minors’ smartphone harms.
- Cost: £8bn pa.

Transport/infrastructure
- Scrap remaining HS2 (one-off £25bn saving); ban ULEZ/CAZ/LTNs; accelerate road/rail upgrades.
- New utility ownership model: 50% public, 50% UK pension funds; cap standing charges.
- Savings: £25bn one-off; £5bn pa.

Agriculture and fisheries
- Farming budget to £3bn; replace climate-linked subsidies with direct payments; reduce red tape; “Buy British” targets.
- Fisheries: license foreign access; expand enforcement; ban supertrawlers; rebuild UK processing and fleets.
- Costs: Agriculture £2bn pa; Fisheries £2bn pa.

Pensions/social care
- Royal Commission on social care; act on offshore tax avoidance in care homes; pension system review; implement Mineworkers Pension recommendations.

Funding summary (claimed)
- Annual savings: £150bn; extra tax from growth: £10bn; total £160bn pa.
- Annual costs: £141bn pa.
